candidates.label: workFeatured

candidates.label: photos

Examples: A hotel has photos of its rooms and amenities. A museum has photos of its exhibits. A city has photos of its various attractions. Distinct from photo, which links to a single photograph.

candidates.label: distinguishingSign

candidates.label: events

Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". candidates.label: workPerformed

candidates.label: subjectOf

candidates.label: alcoholWarning

Examples: "A medication's alcohol warning states 'Do not consume alcohol'.", "The drug's alcohol warning advises 'Limit alcohol intake'."

candidates.label: suggestedAge

Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". candidates.label: recommendedIntake

Examples: "A vitamin supplement has a recommended intake '1 tablet daily for adults'.", "A mineral supplement has a recommended intake '2 capsules twice a day'.", "A protein powder has a recommended intake '30g post-workout'."

candidates.label: suggestedMeasurement

Also called "size recommendation", "body measurement range", "fit guide", "sizing suggestion". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedMeasurement inseam 32-34 inches", "The size specification includes suggestedMeasurement height 170-190 cm", "This product is designed for a suggestedMeasurement chest 40-42 inches."

candidates.label: diseasePreventionInfo

Examples: "Special announcement diseasePreventionInfo 'cdc.gov/prevention'", "Public health alert diseasePreventionInfo 'WebContent on handwashing'", "COVID-19 update diseasePreventionInfo 'who.int/prevention'".

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: recommendationStrength

Also called strength of evidence, guideline strength. Examples: "A medical guideline recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Class I'.", "A treatment guideline has a recommendation strength 'Strong'.", "A diagnostic recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Grade B'."

candidates.label: ccRecipient

candidates.label: suggestedMaxAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the maximum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "maximum age", "upper age limit", "age cap". Examples: "The game has suggestedMaxAge 12", "The audience specification includes suggestedMaxAge 65", "This content is suitable up to suggestedMaxAge 18.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMinAge, which specifies only the minimum.

candidates.label: discussionUrl

candidates.label: subEvent

Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subEvents

Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: partOfTrip

Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: partOfSystem

Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: subStructure

Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". candidates.label: partOfEpisode

candidates.label: superEvent

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: teaches
candidates.comment: An educational relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is designed to teach. Also called "educates on", "imparts knowledge of", "instructs in", "covers topic". Examples: "The course teaches 'Algebra'", "The learning resource teaches problem-solving skills", "This event teaches advanced programming concepts."

candidates.label: geoCovers
candidates.comment: A geo covers relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place completely covers another, meaning every point of the covered entity is within the covering entity. Also called: covers, encompasses, overlies. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo covers "City 'Paris'", "North America" geo covers "Lake 'Superior'", "City 'Springfield'" geo covers "House '123 Main St'". Distinct from geoCoveredBy, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: itemOffered
candidates.comment: A transaction subject relation between a demand or offer and the specific item, product, service, or event being requested or provided. Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.

candidates.label: coverageStartTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage begins. Also called: coverage start, reporting start time, live blog commencement. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage start time "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage start time "2023-07-15T14:00:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage start time "2023-10-27T09:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageEndTime, which indicates when coverage concludes.

candidates.label: aspect
candidates.comment: A specific area or topic of medical practice considered on a medical webpage. Also called: medical topic, health aspect, clinical focus. Examples: "MedicalWebPage 'Diabetes' aspect 'diagnosis'", "MedicalWebPage 'Flu' aspect 'treatment'", "MedicalWebPage 'Cancer' aspect 'prognosis'."

candidates.label: coverageEndTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage concludes. Also called: coverage end, reporting end time, live blog conclusion. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage end time "2024-11-06T04:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage end time "2023-07-15T19:30:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage end time "2023-10-27T17:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageStartTime, which indicates when coverage begins.

relations.definition: Indicates that a subject caused severe and widespread damage to an object.
relations.embedding_query_text: devastated: Indicates that a subject caused severe and widespread damage to an object.

instances: Hurricane Milton -> Tampa, Florida, metropolitan area

chosen_property.label: causesDamageTo
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a geographical region or entity that suffered severe damage caused by an event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures an Event causing severe damage to a geographical region.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard
candidates.comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.

candidates.label: greater
candidates.comment: A greater relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior or larger than another. Also called: is greater than, exceeds, is more than. Examples: "High" greater "Medium", "Excellent" greater "Good", "Large" greater "Small". Distinct from greaterOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

relations.embedding_query_text: occurred at:

instances: student-led protests -> Columbia University

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property directly indicates where an Action takes place, fitting the definition of 'occurred at'.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: foodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

relations.definition: Indicates a health condition or characteristic that increases the risk of a particular outcome or infection.
relations.embedding_query_text: identifies risk factor: Indicates a health condition or characteristic that increases the risk of a particular outcome or infection.

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: A RiskFactorIdentification (CreativeWork) is 'about' the MedicalConditions it identifies as risk factors.

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: includedRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A risk factor inclusion relation between a medical risk estimator and a risk factor used in its calculation. Also called risk factor in calculation, factor considered, included element. Examples: "A medical risk estimator includes a risk factor of age.", "The estimator considers an included risk factor of smoking.", "This tool uses an included risk factor for calculation."

candidates.label: risks
candidates.comment: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.

candidates.label: significance
candidates.comment: The medical or diagnostic importance of superficial anatomy, indicating how its characteristics may suggest underlying conditions or treatments. Also called clinical relevance, diagnostic implication, anatomical importance. Examples: `Skin Lesion` significance `"May indicate melanoma"`, `Swollen Lymph Node` significance `"Could suggest infection"`, `Discolored Nail Bed` significance `"Possible circulatory issue"`.

candidates.label: estimatesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".

candidates.label: epidemiology
candidates.comment: An epidemiology relation between a medical condition or physical activity and the text describing the characteristics of associated patients. Also called "patient demographics", "disease characteristics", "population data". Examples: "Medical condition 'Flu' epidemiology 'Affects all ages, higher risk in elderly and young children'", "Physical activity 'Running' epidemiology 'Common among young adults, higher injury rates in beginners'", "Disease 'Diabetes' epidemiology 'Higher prevalence in certain ethnic groups'".

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: primaryPrevention
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a preventative therapy used to avert the initial occurrence of a medical condition. Also called preventative measure, initial prevention, prophylactic therapy. Examples: A medical condition has a primary prevention of 'vaccination'. Heart disease has a primary prevention of 'healthy diet'. Infection has a primary prevention of 'hand washing'.
